0.long_answer: In cases of severe autosomal recessive hemolytic anemia due to an alpha-spectrin gene mutation, the underlying defect in the red blood cell cytoskeleton leads to the formation of spherocytes, which are more likely to be sequestered and destroyed in the spleen. Splenectomy (the surgical removal of the spleen) alleviates the condition by reducing the extravascular hemolysis that occurs in this organ, thereby mitigating the anemia associated with the disease.
